tagline: From a stone mill in the gap to the forest's edge.
intro: Prince William County's byways keep to its rural edge. In the northwest, Waterfall Road, Antioch Road and SR 55 run out to the county line at Thoroughfare Gap, where they meet the Fauquier County byways. Farther south, Aden Road, Bristow Road and Joplin Road go by way of Nokesville and Brentsville to Independent Hill and the edge of Prince William Forest Park, ending at I-95.
Brentsville was the county seat from 1820 to 1894, and it had a hard war. Union troops took parts of its courthouse apart to build other things.

moments.title: Beverley Mill
moments.text: A five-story stone mill straddling the county line in Thoroughfare Gap, where Broad Run drops 87 feet in 1,300, kept from I-66 in the 1960s when private citizens got the interstate routed around it.

moments.title: Brentsville
moments.text: The old courthouse hamlet was laid out in 1822 with seventy lots, a court house, a clerk's office and a jail, and by 1835 had two taverns to go with them.

moments.title: Prince William Forest Park
moments.text: More than 13,000 acres of Piedmont forest, which in the Second World War was fenced in with barbed wire and used to train spies.
